newsitem.title: USA: TBS puts layoff ceiling at 500-paper.
newsitem.headline: TBS puts layoff ceiling at 500-paper.

text.p: Turner Broadcasting System Inc will lose no more than 500 jobs in its merger with Time Warner Inc, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported on Wednesday.
The newspaper quoted TBS executive vice president Terence McGuirk as saying: "I'd be surprised if it were 500." But he said the company still planned to shave expenses by $100 million.
Company officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.

McGuirk spoke to the Journal-Constitution in New York, after attending a news conference on the 1998 Goodwill Games. The executive will become chairman, president and chief executive officer of TBS Inc under Time Warner, once the merger is completed this fall.
Shareholders of both companies are expected to vote on the merger on October 10 in New York.
Several weeks ago, the newspaper cited an internal TBS report that suggested the owner of Cable News Network could shed up to 1,000 positions in order to save $100 million.
The article said McGuirk believes the money can be saved without job losses of that magnitude. But he said he expected layoffs to number in the hundreds.
